column3: tIdiom::tIdiom(). The class's members and 0x005d392a/0x005d39b7, whose asserts name Idiom.cpp, are one object: with 0x005d39b7's body (string assignment into the vector) in the same source file, the file's copy of vector<string>::operator= (0x0046090a) compiles to the original's 449 bytes, and to 442 without it.
tIdiom's scalar deleting destructor; tIdiom is compiled with 0x005d39b7 (see 0x005d37d2).
tIdiom::tIdiom(const tIdiom&), which calls the vector<string>::operator= copy at 0x0046090a; see 0x005d37d2.

A tIdiom member (thiscall, passes its argument on to 0x005d39b7 with index 0), called by tIdiom::tIdiom(const string&) and from 0x00546dda, so not inlined; it lies before 0x005d3ad9, the next object's first static initializer (each object here starts with one: 0x005d37b1 before tIdiom, 0x005d3b5b before tRelay).

The vector<string>::resize(n, x) instance (insert at 0x00404695, erase at 0x00404044); its one caller is 0x005d39b7, and it lies before 0x005d3ad9, the next object's first static initializer (see 0x005d3a6a).
